grayscale-converter.quickAnswer: Upload a photo and drag the blend slider: 0 keeps full color, 100 gives pure black and white. Each pixel's gray value comes from the standard luminance formula — 0.299 x red + 0.587 x green + 0.114 x blue — so a pixel of (200, 100, 50) becomes gray 124. Download the result as PNG.
keyFacts: Grayscale uses the luminance formula, not a simple average — green counts most because eyes are most sensitive to it.
The blend slider mixes color and gray, so 50 gives a faded vintage wash.

The output PNG keeps full resolution and sharpness.

grayscale-converter.formula:
Luminance (ITU-R BT.601):
gray = 0.299 x R + 0.587 x G + 0.114 x B
Blend:
result = color + (gray - color) x (blend / 100)
At blend = 100, every channel equals gray.
grayscale-converter.workedExample:
Pixel (R=200, G=100, B=50), blend 100:
1. 0.299 x 200 = 59.8.
2. 0.587 x 100 = 58.7.
3. 0.114 x 50 = 5.7.
4. gray = 59.8 + 58.7 + 5.7 = 124.2, rounded to 124.
5. Result pixel: (124, 124, 124) — a neutral mid-gray.
At blend 50 the same pixel would become (162, 112, 87): halfway between color and gray.

faqs.q: Is this a true black-and-white conversion?
faqs.a: Yes. It uses the standard luminance formula (0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B) that cameras and professional editors use, weighted to match human vision. It is not a naive average of the three channels.

faqs.q: What does the blend slider do?
faqs.a: It mixes the original color with the grayscale version. At 100 you get pure black and white; at 50 a faded, desaturated look; at 0 the untouched original. Anything in between is a partial fade.
No. Only color information is removed. Resolution, sharpness, and detail are pixel-identical to the original.

faqs.q: Can I get the color back after downloading?
faqs.a: No — the downloaded PNG genuinely contains only gray pixels. Always keep your original file if you might want color later.

faqs.q: Why do some photos look flat in black and white?
faqs.a: Photos that separate subjects by color rather than brightness lose that separation in gray. Images with strong light-and-shadow contrast convert best. The blend slider lets you keep a hint of color when full B&W falls flat.

faqs.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. Conversion happens pixel by pixel in your browser. Your photo never leaves your device.
